reviewSummary: I resolved every claim from bytes on disk rather than from the dispatch prose or from the draft's own self-description. I recomputed all 11 distinct digests the draft cites and all 11 matched. I recomputed HEAD, the live COORD digest and the live file 08 digest and confirmed all three match the dispatched values with zero working-tree diff on the two tracked governance files. I parsed both Stage A g21-fixture-corpus.v16 reviews and compared field presence, field type and identifier membership against the draft's recitation: the Claude return is a top-level ACCEPT with a string decision, a counts object of 0/0/3/6, three named advisory objects and six named observation objects with the exact member sets recited, and none of the seven fields the draft calls absent are present; the Codex return is a top-level ACCEPT with a string decision, four empty lists, numeric zero counts, findingIdentifiersInvented false and findingIdentifiers empty. Both Stage A reviews carry subject custody on the correct frozen bytes and the Codex review records peerReviewRead false, so the dual ACCEPT is independent. I hex-dumped the one authored fixture: it is exactly four bytes 01 00 00 01, a big-endian unsigned 16777217 with no body, which is the quoted postHandshake ceiling 16777216 plus one and is not a reuse of the 16777216 prefix authored at g21-fixture-corpus.v11; its directory holds that single file and no platform subdirectory, matching the draft's Subject. I read the DR-G21 row in file 08 directly and it is OPEN as claimed, with condition 2 at 5 of 32 and condition 4 MET at 28 of 28, and DR-118 and DR-107 carrying the non-OPEN tokens the draft declines to flatten. I confirmed the predecessor attributions against the recorded headings for D-301, D-302, D-316, D-324 and D-326, and confirmed the G10-occupancy platform recital reproduces wording already adopted in COORD. On wording I found no deictic leftover-join reference, no bare version token, no predecessor-voiced disclaimer, no broken-hyphen artifact of the kind the adopted D-334 draft carried, and no claim contradicted by bytes. Three constructions that could read as defects in isolation — the plural 'findings' for a single unlabeled Codex finding, the no-SATISFY disclaimers split between header and Decision paragraph, and the unwrite list omitting D-243 — each reproduce the adopted precedent at D-334 and D-301 exactly, so I charge none of them. All twelve dispatched attacks are refuted and none is sustained.
decision: CONSENT — 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. Every dispatched attack refuted from bytes; every cited digest recomputed and matched.
